findings.source_passage: Miss Cowley left the delights (and drudgeries) of her home life early in the war and came up to London, where she entered an officers' hospital.
findings.why_it_matters: The parenthetical '(and drudgeries)' and the full mock-formal framing of the biography opening are part of Christie's comic voice; the draft jumps straight to the hospital, erasing the ironic setup sentence that establishes the bit's register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence 'Miss Cowley left the delights (and drudgeries) of her home life early in the war and came up to London, where she entered an officers' hospital.' before the month-by-month list.

findings.source_passage: Eighth month: Slight check in career. Sister Bond ate Sister Westhaven's egg! Grand row! Wardmaid clearly to blame! Inattention in such important matters cannot be too highly censured.
findings.why_it_matters: The mock-bureaucratic sentence 'Inattention in such important matters cannot be too highly censured' is the comic apex of the eighth-month entry and a distinctive voice marker; the draft omits it entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Inattention in such important matters cannot be too highly censured.' after 'Wardmaid clearly to blame!'

findings.source_passage: Tenth month: Reproved by matron for visiting the pictures in company with one of the patients, namely: the aforementioned Lieutenant Thomas Beresford. Eleventh and twelfth months: Parlourmaid duties resumed with entire success.
findings.why_it_matters: The draft condenses 'Eleventh and twelfth months: Parlourmaid duties resumed with entire success' into 'Eleventh and twelfth: Parlourmaid triumph,' losing the mock-formal 'resumed with entire success' phrasing that sustains the comedy of the whole passage.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Parlourmaid duties resumed with entire success' verbatim.

findings.source_passage: After that, the talented Miss Cowley drove successively a trade delivery van, a motor-lorry and a general! The last was the pleasantest. He was quite a young general!
findings.source_locator: End of Tuppence's biography, post-hospital section
findings.why_it_matters: 'The talented Miss Cowley' and 'The last was the pleasantest' are the ironic pay-off of the driving-a-general joke; the draft collapses all three sentences into a single clause and drops the punch-line structure entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'After that, the talented Miss Cowley drove successively…The last was the pleasantest. He was quite a young general!' as three distinct sentences.

findings.source_passage: Tommy shook his head sadly. There was a silence, and then Tuppence burst out: 'Money, money, money! I think about money morning, noon and night! I dare say it's mercenary of me, but there it is!'
findings.source_locator: After Tommy's 'I'm just about desperate' exchange
findings.why_it_matters: The draft compresses 'I dare say it's mercenary of me, but there it is!' and the preceding narrative beat ('Tommy shook his head sadly. There was a silence') into a bald paragraph break, losing both the self-aware ironic qualifier and the rhythmic build-up to the outburst.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'I dare say it's mercenary of me, but there it is!' and the brief narrative bridge before Tuppence's speech.

findings.source_passage: Come now, you can't say I'm sentimental… No one would ever think of sentiment in connection with you. That's not very polite, but I dare say you mean it all right.
findings.source_locator: Marriage discussion, after 'I'm not sentimental, you know'
findings.why_it_matters: This brief exchange neatly characterises the Tommy-Tuppence dynamic and Tuppence's mock-offended self-awareness; its omission slightly flattens the relationship register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the brief back-and-forth: Tuppence's 'Come now, you can't say I'm sentimental' / Tommy's 'No one would ever think of sentiment…' / Tuppence's 'That's not very polite.'

findings.source_passage: the joint venture…makes one think of galleons and doubloons. A joint venture!
findings.why_it_matters: The draft retains 'galleons and doubloons' but omits the fuller explanation ('musty old figures…It's got an Elizabethan flavour about it') that gives the romantic digression its self-mocking texture.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'such a romantic phrase to come across in the middle of musty old figures. It's got an Elizabethan flavour about it' before 'galleons and doubloons.'

summary: Four medium-severity findings (key comic sentences in Tuppence's mock-biography systematically flattened, the 'mercenary of me' self-qualifier dropped, and the parlourmaid close-out paraphrased) collectively constitute voice erasure of the chapter's most signature set-piece and trigger regeneration.
